metaTitle: Asbestos Removal Cost Guide Geelong | Barwon Asbestos Co
metaDescription: What asbestos removal really costs around Geelong: a minimum job charge of $800 to $1,500, whole fences $1,000 to $3,500, roofs $40 to $120 a square metre.
h1: What Asbestos Removal Costs in Geelong and the Barwon Region
heroSub: Nobody publishes a Geelong price list for this work. What does exist is a set of Victorian rates, a minimum job charge that explains most small quotes, and a short list of things that move the number up or down.
introHtml:
The most useful number on this page is not a rate per square metre. It is the minimum job charge. Victorian removalists publish a minimum of $800 to $1,500 for a residential job, and it explains most of the quotes that catch people off guard. The gap between two cracked sheets off a shed wall and a whole fence line is much smaller than you would expect, because the bulk of the cost is simply getting a licensed crew and a legal disposal load to your address.

Every figure here comes from Victorian suppliers, councils or national cost guides. None of them is a quote from us, and none is a Geelong rate, because no Geelong or Barwon operator publishes one. Read them as Melbourne metro benchmarks; two of those suppliers price regional work separately anyway. Prices are indicative and GST treatment varies between providers, so ask each removalist whether their quote includes GST.

sections.heading: What actually moves the number
sections.html:
Area is the obvious driver and the easiest to estimate. Two independent Victorian suppliers put general non-friable removal at $45 to $150 per square metre, agreeing within $5 at the bottom and exactly at the top of that band. Where you land inside it has less to do with the size of the job than with everything around it.

Condition matters more than area. Sheeting that is sound is non-friable, which is Class B work. Material that has gone chalky and crumbly, been through a fire, or already been smashed can be treated as friable, and friable asbestos is Class A work with no exemption at any quantity. Nobody publishes a reliable price difference between the two, so be wary of any site that gives you one.

The rest is logistics, and it is where two quotes on the same amount of material pull apart. These are the things a removalist is weighing up when they look at your place:

  • How much there is, and whether it comes off in whole sheets or has already been broken
  • Working height, roof pitch, and whether a truck can get down the side of the house
  • How far the material has to be carried to the vehicle
  • Total weight going to the tip, because disposal is charged by the tonne
  • Whether a clearance certificate is needed, which is a separate third party cost

Lead time is worth planning for, even though it is not a line on the quote. A licence holder has to notify WorkSafe before starting: at least 24 hours ahead for 10 square metres or less of non-friable material, and at least five days ahead for anything larger. That duty sits with the removalist, never with you, and it is the usual reason a crew cannot start tomorrow.

sections.heading: Why a two sheet repair is not a two sheet price
sections.html:
Per sheet rates of $20 to $50 circulate widely and they are real, but read on their own they are misleading. On a four sheet repair you are not paying $200. You are paying the minimum job charge of $800 to $1,500, because the cost sits in the setup rather than the sheets.

That setup is the same whether the job is small or large. A controlled work area, protective equipment, keeping the material wet, taking sheets off whole instead of breaking them, wrapping everything to the required thickness of plastic, labelling every package, and carting a legal load to a landfill licensed to accept it. A full set of eaves, which is a fiddly job at height, sits at $1,500 to $2,500 for much the same reason.

Worth knowing if you have more than one thing to deal with. If a removalist is already coming for the fence, ask them to price the shed wall, the old eaves lining and the garage roof in the same visit. Mobilisation is the expensive part and you only pay for it once.

sections.heading: The lines on a quote people do not expect
sections.html:
Disposal is the big one. Asbestos waste is classified as reportable priority waste in Victoria and can only go to a landfill authorised to receive it. In the whole Barwon region there is exactly one: Drysdale Landfill, small domestic quantities only, with a six by four trailer as the cap. Call them on (03) 5251 2935 before you load anything, because authorised landfills can still decline a load and you may need to book a time.

Drysdale does not publish its asbestos fee, so anyone quoting you a Geelong gate price is guessing. Other Victorian councils do publish theirs, at $100 to $376 per tonne, a spread of nearly four times across three shires. That spread is the reason a single Victorian disposal figure would be wrong for most of the state, and none of those three is Geelong. Every Surf Coast transfer station refuses asbestos and Colac Otway publishes no option at all, so a Torquay or Colac homeowner is looking at one legal destination on the Bellarine, which the disposal page covers properly.

Then there is the clearance certificate. It runs $165 to $250 and it has to come from an independent person, someone with no financial interest in the removal, which means it can never be the removalist who did the work. It is required after Class A or Class B removal, and not required where the job was only non-friable material not exceeding 10 square metres in total. For a homeowner at their own home the duty to obtain it sits with the licence holder, not with you.

Air monitoring is the line most often quoted at people who do not need it. It runs $250 to $600 per day where it is required, and Victoria's regulations do not require it for Class B work. On an ordinary residential fence or roof it is not a routine cost.

Skip bins, last. No Victorian operator publishes an asbestos bin price, so anyone quoting you one is quoting, not publishing. What is consistent is the structure: a hire fee plus a separate tipping fee charged by weight, with the bin lined and the material bagged before it goes in. Asbestos never goes in a general waste skip or out with a council hard waste collection.

sections.heading: Doing it yourself, and what the law actually says
sections.html:
This is the part most cost guides get wrong, and getting it wrong costs people money. The limits you will read everywhere, 10 square metres of non-friable material and no more than one hour of removal work in any seven days, come from Victoria's OHS Regulations. They bind employers and self-employed persons at workplaces. A home is not a workplace, so they do not apply to a homeowner working on their own house, and it is not accurate to say it is illegal to remove more than 10 square metres at home.

What is accurate is more useful anyway. That is the limit the law sets for anyone doing this as work, WorkSafe recommends homeowners follow the same code, and both caps become law the moment a tradesperson, a tenant, a rental property, business premises or a paid helper is involved. Friable material is never covered at any quantity and always needs a Class A removalist.

So the honest answer on saving money: a fence line, a garage or a house roof is far past 10 square metres and far past an hour of work regardless of who does it. The saving is also smaller than it looks once you price plastic of the right thickness, labelled packaging, a vehicle you are willing to line, and the single legal destination on the Bellarine. Testing is where the real money is saved, at $88 to $160 per sample, because it tells you whether any of this applies before you spend anything. Get it tested before you touch it, and call now if you want us to put you in touch with licensed asbestos removalists whose WorkSafe Victoria licence number appears on their quote.

faq.q: How much does asbestos removal cost in Geelong?
faq.a: There is no published Geelong or Barwon price for this work, so the honest answer is a Victorian range and the things that move it. General non-friable removal runs $45 to $150 per square metre, a whole fibro fence $1,000 to $3,500, and a house roof $4,000 to $15,000. Underneath all of it sits a minimum job charge of $800 to $1,500, which is what most small jobs actually cost. Those are Melbourne metro benchmarks published by suppliers and cost guides, not quotes from us.

faq.q: Why is there a minimum charge on a small job?
faq.a: Because the cost is in the setup, not the sheeting. A licensed crew still has to establish a controlled work area, keep the material wet, take it off in whole sheets, wrap and label every package to the required standard, and cart a legal load to a landfill licensed to accept asbestos. That is the same work for four sheets as for forty. It is why per sheet rates of $20 to $50 only make sense read against the $800 to $1,500 minimum.

It varies, and we will not pretend otherwise. Some of the suppliers behind these figures publish prices including GST, some exclude it, and several do not say either way, so we cannot put a single GST label on any range here. Prices are indicative and GST treatment varies between providers, so ask each removalist whether their quote includes GST. Ask for it in writing alongside their WorkSafe Victoria licence number.

faq.q: What does it cost just to find out whether it is asbestos?
faq.a: Lab analysis runs $88 to $160 per sample, and most houses need three to eight samples, because every different material has to be tested separately. A fence, an eaves lining and a bathroom wall sheet are three samples, not one. Standard turnaround is 1 to 5 business days, with a surcharge of 25% to 50% for a 24 to 48 hour result. Compared with everything else on this page, testing is cheap, and it is the only step that tells you whether the rest applies.

faq.q: Does a removal quote cover replacing what comes off?
faq.a: No, and you should expect two separate trades. A removal quote covers taking the material off, wrapping it, transporting it and disposing of it legally. The new fence, the re-cladding or the re-roofing is building work that you arrange separately with a registered builder, and we never price it. Be careful with any all-in removal and replacement figure you see online, because it hides which half of the job you are actually being quoted for.
